title: Quality gates for catalog updates & customer version locks (auto-run evaluations)
creator: Riley Patel
description:
Goal: Ensure any change that modifies the public model catalog or a customer-locked (version-locked) model automatically runs a targeted quality suite before the change is promoted to production routes. This ticket defines the product requirements, acceptance criteria, and rollout plan for gating catalog updates and customer version locks with automated evaluations that surface regressions and block unsafe rollouts.

Scope:
- Trigger targeted evaluation jobs when a catalog entry is updated (model binary, quantization profile, or default config changes).
- Trigger evaluation jobs when a customer creates/updates a version lock (customer-locked model).
- Support configurable evaluation profiles: smoke (fast), regression (moderate), and full (extended) tied to change type and customer SLA.
- Integrate results with the Console: show eval scores, diffs vs baseline, and provide a one-click rollback or force-approve option guarded by ACL.

Non-goals:
- Not implementing new eval metrics from scratch (we will reuse existing eval harness and probes).
- Not changing billing model for evaluations in this phase (costs are charged to the change initiator's project).

Acceptance criteria:
1) Catalog edits in the Console or API create an eval job that runs the appropriate profile and stores results in the eval service.
2) Customer version locks via API/Console trigger the same eval flow.
3) If evals flag a regression above configured thresholds, the change is marked as blocked and an actionable alert is shown with diffs and suggested rollback.
4) Operators can configure default profiles per catalog entry and per customer via the Console.
5) Audit logs capture who approved forced overrides and which eval artifacts were used.
6) End-to-end latency for smoke profile <= 5 minutes for typical model/seed set.

Metrics to track:
- Fraction of catalog/customer-lock changes that run an eval (target 100%).
- Regression detection rate and false positive rate (aim FP < 5%).
- Mean time from change to eval-completion for smoke/regression profiles.
- Number of blocked rollouts prevented by automated evals.

Trade-offs and decisions:
- Frequency vs cost: we will default to smoke-profile for minor config edits to limit cost; full profile reserved for major model binaries or customer-requested locks.
- Production vs staging evals: by default run evals in staging infra against production-like data; for high-SLA customers offer an option to run evaluations in a private/air-gapped environment (separate ticket).
- Blocking policy: default block on >THRESHOLD regression for customer-locked changes; for catalog changes block only for high-impact models (popularity tier) unless the author sets stricter policy.

Rollout plan:
1) Build API hooks and event listeners in the catalog service to emit eval triggers (ENG implements).
2) Expose profile selection and override UI in Console (Product/Design).
3) Wire eval orchestration and store results; add dashboards and alerts (Observability).
4) Pilot with 10 internal teams and 3 beta customers, iterate threshold tuning.
5) Full rollout with telemetry & playbook for on-call.

Open questions: 
- What should the default regression threshold be for text-gen vs embeddings? (engineering proposal pending).
- Do we charge customers for evaluation runs by default or include a free quota? (commercial discussion needed).
- Should forced-approve actions require SSO-based 2nd approval for high-impact models? (security input requested).
acceptance_criteria: Eval automatically created for catalog edit via Console/API
Eval automatically created for customer version lock actions
Blocked state applied when regression exceeds configured thresholds
Console shows eval diffs and one-click rollback/force-approve
Audit trail recorded for approvals and overrides
Smoke profile completes under 5 minutes in staging
implementation_notes: Catalog service will emit a 'model_change.v1' event with metadata (model_id, change_type, baseline_version)
Eval-orchestrator will accept event and map to profile; use existing probe sets from /evals/probes/catalog
Console will add a 'Quality' tab on catalog entries showing recent eval runs, trend sparkline, and latest status
Permissions: only users with 'catalog:approve' may force-approve blocked changes; log user + rationale
risks: Cost blowup if full-profile is accidentally applied to large binary changes; mitigate by limiting who can select full-profile
False positives could block benign rollouts — need good probe coverage and rapid override path
Long eval latency may slow small config changes; provide asynchronous promotion option for non-blocking edits
